text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.4% today, continuing a recovery from a steep four-day sell-off that had knocked the stock down 5.2% since mid-September. The bounce reflects cautious optimism in oil markets—crude rose Thursday as traders weighed reports that Asia may be importing record volumes of oil and that a phased reopening of the Hormuz Strait (a critical shipping chokepoint) is under discussion, suggesting potential de-escalation in Middle East tensions. However, oil's gains remain capped; the wider geopolitical risk and uncertainty over U.S. policy on diesel exports (which could constrain refiner margins and fuel supply) are keeping investors from betting too heavily on energy stocks right now.

The stock's recovery is tentative against a backdrop of conflicting pressures. High diesel prices ($6.51 per gallon nationally, nearly triple last year's levels) are drawing warnings from industry and political figures about export restrictions, but any near-term policy clarity remains absent—leaving refiners and oil producers in a holding pattern.
